turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, have a seat. What can I do for you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, so the headaches. I've had migraines for years, but lately they're different, worse when I first wake up, and—
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long's lately?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, and the missus reckons I snore all night and I'm wrecked, but she's—
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): The headaches. Weeks or months?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, sorry. About three weeks. Maybe four. We'd just got back from Merimbula, lovely spot, the bakery there does this—
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Three or four weeks. Vomiting with them?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, yeah, twice. Both times first thing in the morning, with the really bad head. I thought it was the prawns from the servo, but—
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only twice?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Twice. Nothing since Sunday.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any change in your vision? Blurring, double vision?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Work's been mental. I'm a chippy, we're short two blokes, and the boss keeps—
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your eyes. Any change?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Nah. Eyes are fine. I can read the plans, no worries.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weakness, numbness, or slurred speech?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Neck stiff at all?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really, no.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still the old migraine? One side, throbbing?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly the right side, yeah, pounding. Light still bugs me, same as always. Just the mornings are new. And the chucking.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many years have you had migraines?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Since I was about twenty-two. So, twenty-odd years. Mum had them worse, poor thing, she'd be in a dark room for days.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What do you take?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan. The fifty— wait, no, I thought the chemist gave me the hundred milligram ones, but the box says fifty.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many days a week?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Most days lately. Actually, more like four or five days a week. And Panadol as well, two of the five hundred milligram tablets, sometimes three times a day.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's a lot of sumatriptan. Anything else?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Nah, that's the lot. I was on propranolol years back, for prevention, but I stopped. Made me feel flat as a tack.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did you stop it?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Ages ago. Before covid, I reckon. Couldn't tell you the year.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergies?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I can take whatever.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smoke? Drink?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Gave up smoking, ten years now. Couple of beers on the weekend, that's it. And I'm not tired, whatever she says. I don't snore.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Recent knock to the head?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Nah. Nearly stacked the ute coming off the highway last month, the dog went flying, but I didn't—
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): No head injury.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Just a near thing. Shook me up more than anything.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll check the nerves. Follow my finger.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): This the follow-the-finger bit? My brother reckons you lot love that. He had a knee done and they still—
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pupils are equal and they react to light. No double vision looking side to side. Grip's strong, both hands.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): See? I'm fine.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Legs push off normally. Finger to nose is accurate. Reflexes are normal. Neck's supple, no stiffness there.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): So it's not a tumour? I googled morning headaches and it all went a bit—
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I didn't say that. Pattern's changed, worse on waking, vomited twice. Could still be migraine, possibly medication overuse, but I can't exclude something intracranial.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. So you're booking a scan?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the morning headaches or the vomiting are still going in two weeks, I'll organise a CT of the head.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. What do I do till then? Because the Panadol's just sitting in the—
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cut sumatriptan to no more than two days in a week. Paracetamol, two tablets, maximum four times a day. And I want you back here in two weeks regardless.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Even if it's settled by then?

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Two weeks, and reception will book it. If you get weakness, confusion, a sudden thunderclap headache, or vomiting you can't keep fluids down, go to emergency. Don't wait for me.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, alright. I'll tell her to ease up about the snoring. She's been winding me up all—
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. We're done.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

bad.reason: Transcript reports wife says he snores all night; extracted absent snoring conflicts.

omissions.text: Patient reported being 'wrecked' / tired, with wife saying he snores all night; this concern was raised early despite later patient denial of tiredness/snoring.
Vomiting episodes were both first thing in the morning with the really bad headache.
Sumatriptan dose was uncertain from the patient's perspective: he said he thought he had 100 mg tablets but the box says 50 mg.
Paracetamol/Panadol current use is two 500 mg tablets per dose, sometimes three times a day; the recorded frequency '2 tablets' is incorrect because that is the dose, not the frequency.
Propranolol was stopped because it 'made me feel flat as a tack' (adverse effect/reason for discontinuation).
Doctor advised return in two weeks regardless, even if symptoms have settled; reception will book it.
